terms.context: A single note the user adds to or edits on a block
terms.notes: Same spelling as English; feminine (une note, la note). Lowercase unless starting a sentence.

terms.context: A paragraph, list item, heading, table row or code block that a note attaches to
The panel listing every note in the file; section heading "The notes list"
terms.notes: Heading is capitalized as "La liste des notes"; in running prose it is lowercase "la liste des notes".

terms.context: Bottom bar showing confirmation messages such as "Note added"
terms.notes: The section heading itself is "Messages d'état", but the element is referred to as "la barre d'état" throughout the prose.

terms.context: The bar at the top of the main window holding File, Edit, View, Notes, Help
Section heading "Using a screen reader" and related prose (JAWS, NVDA)
terms.notes: Heading rendered as "Utiliser un lecteur d'écran".

terms.context: The opening/closing marker text (e.g. [usernote]/[/usernote]) surrounding a note; "changing the markers"
terms.notes: Masculine (un marqueur, le marqueur). "Changing the markers" warning is rendered "changer les marqueurs".

terms.context: A Markdown checklist item; "Mark this task as done?"
The Document language setting controlling the voice/encoding assumptions for the open file
terms.notes: Exact capitalization used for the setting label and menu item; lowercase "langue du document" in running prose.

terms.context: The Interface language setting controlling the language of menus, dialogs and messages
terms.notes: Exact capitalization used for the setting label and menu item; lowercase "langue de l'interface" in running prose.

terms.context: Generic word for a dialog box, e.g. the Open dialog or a yes/no confirmation
terms.notes: Feminine (une boîte de dialogue, la boîte de dialogue). French spells this word with a final -e, unlike the American English 'dialog'.

terms.context: The buttons on PlanCake's yes-or-no confirmation dialogs (DialogHelper.Confirm)
Windows Explorer, e.g. dragging a file from it, or its "Copy as path" command
terms.notes: Official French Windows name for the app; capitalized as a proper noun.

terms.context: The Windows Downloads folder that downloaded plans are saved to
terms.notes: "Téléchargements" kept capitalized as the actual French Windows folder name.

terms.context: The Windows Start menu, used to launch PlanCake
terms.notes: "Démarrer" capitalized as the official Windows button/menu name; "menu" lowercase.

terms.context: Windows cmd.exe, e.g. "the plancake command works in any new PowerShell or Command Prompt window"
terms.notes: Rendered as a lowercase common noun ("invite de commandes"), not capitalized as a product name the way the English manual capitalizes "Command Prompt".

terms.translation: Copier en tant que chemin d'accès
terms.context: File Explorer's "Copy as path" command, which wraps the copied path in quotation marks
A GitHub issue: "Paste them into a new issue on PlanCake's GitHub page"
terms.notes: "New issue" rendered as "un nouveau ticket", not a literal translation of "issue".

terms.context: The GitHub "Raw" link/button used to reach a file's raw Markdown
terms.notes: Left untranslated: GitHub's own UI does not localize this button/label either.
